en: The Table of Contents for the Recorded Sayings of Master Xuzhou:
The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master [Xuzhou] at Baoning Chan Temple in Banzhang, Jiankang Prefecture.
Recorded Sayings of Longyou Chan Temple on Mount Jinshan, Zhenjiang Prefecture;
Recorded Sayings of Baozhong Chan Temple at Lüyuan, Tanzhou;
Recorded Sayings of Baiyun Chan Temple at Shushan, Fuzhou.
Record of the Sayings of the Chengtian Nengren Chan Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture;
Record of the Sayings of the Zhongtianzhu Tiantai Ningwanshou Yongzu Chan Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture;
Record of the Sayings of the Lingyin Jingde Chan Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture.
Record of Sermons, Minor Lectures, Verses, Eulogies, Self-Eulogies, Minor Rituals, and Biographical Epilogues from Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Temple at Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture.
(Jong-lin) In years past, he traveled across the sea to the Song dynasty, traveling back and forth between Wu and Yue.
He frequently attended his former teacher at the lakes and mountains of Lin-an, where he constantly listened to the "talk by the brazier" and occasionally recounted the master’s former exhortations.

Because these teachings had not yet been permitted for circulation among students, they were recorded only by Zhieruo; they consist merely of the discourses from two assemblies at Caizhu Peak and Lingshan.

Having been separated from Master De for thirty years, I have long harbored a deep and poignant regret at not having seen his full chapters and complete works. Unexpectedly, I have now suddenly obtained the records of eight assemblies.
I have recorded it in its entirety. Overjoyed beyond measure, I could not let go of the scroll from my hand.

Observing its phrasing and the tone of its prose—concise, archaic, and with a sharp, incisive wit—it was as if I were sitting at his side, personally hearing his exhortations. Truly, he is a banner of light for the Dharma-ending age.

Yet, fearing deeply that this work might fall into oblivion, I considered it my duty as one who comes after him to ensure its survival; thus, I commissioned craftsmen to carve it into printing blocks so that it may endure forever.

If, upon reading this, one comes to know that there was the Great Master Songyuan and his authentic lineage of transmission, who could say that this does not benefit the school? If you say otherwise, consider this:
before Zhang Zai (Zi Yun) was born, for a desolate millennium, was it truly the case that there were no *Taixuan* or *Fayan* treatises in the world?
Written on the day of the winter solstice during the first year of the Jiayuan era by the junior dharma-heir of Shan’an (Qionglin).
Recorded from the discourse records of Venerable Xuzhou of the Great Song, successor to the Dharma at Lingyin Chan Monastery in Hangzhou; compiled by Jingfu.
When the Master first entered Baonan Chan Temple on Mount Ban at Jiankang Prefecture, he pointed to the mountain gate and said:
"In front, no shops are built; behind, no villages are clustered. Facing the sun, it cuts off all passage; above and below, it is evenly divided. Look further:
it penetrates straight through to the very peak of the clouds, walking alone across the universe."
The Buddha Hall: Awakening to the Way, one is stained by mud and sand; Buddhas and Patriarchs become one's enemies. New Banzhan, why do you burn incense and prostrate?
A bright pearl is free of flaws; white jade is without blemish.
Sitting cross-legged in the hall, there is host and guest; there is neither distance nor intimacy. Even if the Seven Buddhas were to arrive, each would receive thirty blows of the staff.
Why? Because they are fond of little and prone to much anger.
Seizing the official decree, he wrests the pivot of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; he assists the hand of Yulin.
Like the *huangzhong* and *dalu* bells, like the *baixue* and *yangchun* songs—how many are there who hear sound with their eyes?
He ascends the seat. Having finished offering incense and making prayers for the Emperor, he says:
"When one Buddha appears in the world, a thousand Buddhas offer praise; cutting off the ten directions, the True Constant alone is revealed."
The mountains are azure; the clouds are azure. Half-open, half-closed, their concealment and manifestation are fully revealed.
If you all can comprehend it in this very way, then the first round of my tenure at Xinshanbàn will be concluded.
Should you not yet have realized this, by the bridge of Zhongshan the sun lingers long, and the swallows fly before the halls of the Wangs and Xies.
Again, he raised the point: "The Way of the Three Sages is: 'When I meet a person, I come forth; when I come forth, I do not act for others. The Way of Xinghua is:
'When I meet a person, I do not come forth; when I come forth, I immediately act for others. The Master took up his staff and said:
"With one eye and one arm alike, there is no lack of these two great elders in upholding the true lineage of Linji. Yet, when examined closely, they are both excellent."
He gave thirty blows with his staff. At New Ban-shan, "Righteousness brings forth a bountiful year. He let the matter pass by one move, leaned on his staff, and descended from the seat.
Entering the hall, he held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying: "This staff has no front or back; it leans east and props west, and climbs the mountain."
"Crossing the sea—the Bian-king jade and the Li-pearl, the lump of mud and the clod of earth. [He strikes the meditation staff once. "All at once, they are pulverized.
[He strikes the meditation staff once again. "The story remains."
The Buddha ascended the hall for the occasion of his *nirvāṇa*. Holding up his staff, he said, "There is one matter that you all must not remain ignorant of.
Śākyamuni the Old Man struck the ground once with the staff and said, "The life-root has been severed! What need is there to speak of 'existing today' or 'non-existing tomorrow'?
Here, on the spring mountains, the *zhègū* birds cry out."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The superior person, hearing the Way, practices it with diligence—beating three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred blows in the evening.

The mediocre person, hearing the Way, treats it as if it were present one moment and gone the next—like a family afflicted by a potent poison that does not even taste its water. The inferior person, hearing the Way, laughs at it loudly."

When the sweet melon reaches the stem, it is sweet; when the bitter gourd is connected to the root, it is bitter. When Ban-shan proclaims in this manner, there are many who nod their heads in defiance.
But in the end, what of it? He hews down the old pine tree before his gate and has it burned for three or five years.
On the Buddha’s Birthday, he ascended the hall. Śākyamuni, as soon as he was born, declared: "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored. Who would have known there was still Old Yunmen?
Though he sits here, a single blow of the staff cannot kill him; even today, after a thousand ages, it remains a scar. Everyone, tell me:
is this gratitude, or is it one of the five heinous crimes? He strikes the meditation staff once and says: "All!"
"One who has departed cannot be given even a single ladle of foul water.
He ascended the hall: "Transcending names and words, surpassing past and present; the Buddha-body is unconditioned and does not fall into any numerical categories. Thus it is, thus it is."
Then it is easy. If it is not so, and not so, then it is difficult. Since the Buddha-body is unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), why is there difficulty and ease?
Have you not heard it said: "The sweet melon is sweet all the way to its stem; the bitter gourd is bitter even to its roots"?

Ascending the hall: The rain washes away the scorching heat; autumn clouds drift at their own ease. One or two flakes upon the tip of my staff, sometimes curling and sometimes unfurling beyond the forest trees.
White jade and bright pearls, lumps of mud and clods of earth—letting go and gathering in, every single one perfectly round.
Filling the ditches and blocking the gullies, no one understands. Aha! Six dice, all red in the bowl. Whether they show a winning face or not.
Everyone, do not compete.
On the Double Ninth, he ascends the hall to speak of Chan and speak of the Way, scattering earth and scattering sand. Ban-shan ultimately does not follow the heterodox;
the Double Ninth is fixed on the ninth day of the ninth month. Where in the eastern hedge is there no yellow chrysanthemum? If it is thus, then matters arise from being cautioned.
Arise! Return to the hall for tea. Ascending the hall, he said:
"To pry open the jaw of a black dragon, the intent is to obtain the pearl; to break the pit of a peach, one must see its kernel.
Now that the kernel is seen, what of the pearl? He struck his staff once and said: "The sea deity knows it is precious, but does not know its price. He left it at that.
Illuminating the Night with Human Radiance.
Recorded Sayings of the Chan Master of Longyou Chan Temple on Mount Jinshan in Zhenjiang Prefecture.
Compiled by Jingfu, Dharma Heir of Lingyin Chan Temple in Hangzhou.
The Master entered the monastery and, pointing to the mountain gate, said: "The Dragon Gate rises ten thousand fathoms high; those who reach it are rare indeed.
Without disturbing the clear waves, how can one advance further? He let out a shout.
The Buddha Hall. What is that which stands? What is that which sits? Holding up his sitting mat, he said: "It does not go beyond this. Entering the room, he struck the sounding block and said:
"The life-force of the Buddhas of the past; the legacy of the Buddhas of the future. To open one's mouth is to perish; to close one's mouth is an error. He struck the sounding block once more.
With one blow of his staff, he said: "To cure an illness, one does not need medicine carried by a donkey.

Taking up the official document, he declared: "A hair’s breadth is no light matter; a mountain is no heavy burden. Pressing down on the cloud-heads of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and piercing through the nostrils of the monks, he split them open so that they may know there is no seam or gap.
The Dharma Seat: taking the emptiness of all phenomena as one’s seat. This has already been established as the model and the pattern.
New Jinshan will never follow along with others. (He lets out a shout.)
He ascends the seat. Having finished offering incense and making prayers for the Emperor, he says:

"Pointing a finger across the river, the myriad phenomena and the ten thousand beings smile and nod their heads. Washing one's feet and boarding the boat, the iron walls and silver mountains are all toppled over.
Thus one sees that there is no standing upon isolation or peril; it is utterly beyond climbing or grasping, cutting off all streams."
How could one allow for convergence? Let loose a single thread, and heaven is level, earth is level; waves are stilled and winds are calm.
Fish and dragons dance in joy—at such a time as this, what is it like? All stars bow toward the North; no water does not flow toward the East.
Again, it is recorded that Minister Li Ao asked Zen Master Yaoshan, "What is the Way?
Yaoshan pointed to the sky and then pointed to a water jar, saying, "Do you understand? Li said, "I do not understand. Yaoshan said, "Clouds in the blue sky; water in the jar.
Li attained great enlightenment and thereupon offered this verse: "My body has been refined until it resembles the form of a crane; Beneath a thousand pine trees, two cases of scripture."
"I have come to ask about the Way; please speak without reserve. "The clouds are in the blue sky; the water is in the pitcher. The Master commented:

"To hold up the sun and moon of Confucius with one's hands and to gird on the true seal of Vairocana at the waist—Noble Minister Li is certainly no lack of these. However, as for the meaning of Yaoshan..."

[The Master] had not yet appeared when he ascended the hall for the Yuanxiao Festival. "One lamp, a thousand lamps; a thousand lamps, one lamp. [He continued,] "This still leaves you sitting within the shadows and reflections.
Holding his whisk, he drew a circle in the air and said, "As for this very thing—is it inside? Is it outside? After a long silence, he spoke again.
"Blind! When Master Chijue arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "The broken sand-pot has no handle; all the people in the great earth cannot support it.
Along the road to Yushan, the thorns reach the heavens; before Mount Zhongfu, the pure wind sweeps the earth. [He] splits open the treasure..."
Master Gongmian’s skin was thick; De-yun had no place to hide. Why? Because it is only natural that it should be so. He ascended the hall and said:
"Before the fifteenth day, we allow only the Old Barbarian to know; we do not allow the Old Barbarian to understand.
After the fifteenth day, we allow only the Old Barbarian to understand; we do not allow the Old Barbarian to know. On the very fifteenth day itself—do you understand, or do you not?"
Knowing and not knowing. The breeze is gentle; the sun lingers. [The Master] strikes the meditation staff once and says: "I would not spare my gold to make this pellet;
beneath the peony flowers, I strike the yellow oriole."
The former monk Daoju arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "The great ocean stirs up dust; the high source pours forth water. Meeting on a narrow path—who among you knows my heart?
Clearly manifest within the light of the jade mirror, vast and boundless are the smoke-waves across ten thousand li. The phoenix raises its head; the golden-scaled dragon flails its tail.
When north of the river and south of the river all hope is lost, a clap of thunder and a clear breeze arise."
Ascending the hall: It cannot be pushed away, nor can it be drawn back. To the south is Tiantai; to the north is Wutai. The vast earth is desolate—what, then, accords with the heart?
The spring breeze sweeps on, as rain beats upon the moss. This is a ready-made koan, not involving any contrived arrangement.
How could it be that one must see peach blossoms before the eyes are opened?
[The Master] ascends the hall: "Clouds gather and sea-mountains loom; the moon reflects as the river and sky break into dawn. Amidst the bustling red dust, how much of the springtime remains?
When the iron walls and silver mountains are pierced open with a single thrust, falling flowers and flowing waters are left to wander in vain. He lets out a shout: "Is it?"
What words can be spoken?

It is only Yang Hui who, while simultaneously thanking [the master] for wielding the whisk and presiding over the ritual, ascends the hall. Where the staff and shouts fly back and forth, whether the teaching is fully raised or only half-raised, this is true diligence;
this is called the true offering of Dharma. Only those who can split open Dongshan’s iron dainty will truly know it. Sit!
Behold Yangzhou as he returns across the crane; at the ancient ferry of Guazhou, facing the slanting glow of the setting sun.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Today is the fifth day of the fifth month; everywhere the drums are sounding. They do not speak of medicine and illness treating one another, but instead speak of writing talismans and chanting incantations over earth.
Since I possess no such skills as those of Mount Jin, I cannot help but travel another path. He struck his staff once.
The text below says:
"When the sun is at its zenith, the Prefect knows to return and bestow fields and manors. Ascending the hall, he sees it all at once; once attained, it is attained forever.
The boundaries on all four sides are thus clearly defined. With a single inch of brush-tip, there is the force of ten thousand *qun*. For thirty years, the strange sprouts have flourished.

Flourishing! Throughout ten thousand ages, he has achieved magnificent deeds amidst the current of history. A-he-he! Do you know or not? The green felt mat was originally a possession of my own house.
Behold well the time when the golden ox dances.
Ascending the hall on the first day of Autumn: Within the shadows of the fiery clouds, a single leaf falls; amidst the radiance of the jade mirror, autumn is seen at once.

Let autumn come as it will and go as it may; the great river flows eastward as ever. There is no change, yet there is a reason for its coming. Where are the wild geese? White egrets on the azure isles.
The evening smoke-village resounds with the whistles of fishermen; scattered are the lingering clouds, and idle are the fishing boats.
A shout! Entering the hall:
The rain washes away the scorching heat; autumn polishes the celestial expanse. The wind carries the fragrance of ripening grain; with bellies full, they sit by the cold crags.
The position shifts and merit returns as the wooden horse neighs; beyond the kalpas, there is no need to seek companions again. (A shout. Circulating the hall for tea.
Entering the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: The sack’s mouth opens and heaven and earth are vast; does the brow of Cuiyan exist or not? One sound—
The wild geese at the Sea Gate in autumn; the traveler is already beyond the green mountains. Entering the hall:
A thousand explanations, ten thousand explanations, are not as good as seeing for oneself. Sometimes there are surging, rolling billows;
sometimes the water is clear and the moon appears. The wind whistles and howls coldly. Although it is the old pavilion’s idle ground, one must win it back once more before it is truly one's own.
The session begins. Entering the hall: The moon is cold, the sky is high; the wind howls amidst the raging surges. Wielding the sword that kills, employing the blade that gives life.

Clouds drift thin over the cold river where wild geese cast their shadows; mountains stretch vast as the setting sun reveals a precarious nest. The subject is already established—just blink your eyebrows.
To suddenly cease ten thousand affairs and return home is also but a labor in vain.

(He gives a shout. Entering the hall, he takes up his staff and shows it to the assembly, saying: "When one reaches the point of speaking, one does not reach the point of practice; when one reaches the point of practice, one does not reach the point of speaking.

One gazes with bated breath toward Penglai, yet the Weak Waters stretch for thirty thousand li. Even if one were to reach both the point of speaking and the point of practice, Jinshan’s staff has still not arrived."
"You all have eaten your fill. Why? If one lacks the strength to lift the cauldron and pull up the mountain, even a thousand-li black steed is not easy to ride.

On the Winter Solstice, he ascended the hall: "The masses of yin are completely stripped away; the single yang returns. The flowers bloom upon the iron trees, their fragrant scent rich and pervasive."
Whether the eyelids are open or closed, south of the branches and again north of the branches; concave and convex, broken sand-pots—how are they like the great radish of Zhenzhou?
Entering the hall: On the festival of Qingming and Hanshi, when the spring light is in full bloom, wild flowers obscure the ancient path; turning back my head, the evening...
The clouds hang low; where the paper money flies, the cuckoo cries. Those who have not undergone bitter toil do not understand.
*Heh!* (A shout). "Fruit-land rice and cloth.
Entering the hall, he said: "To speak a ten-foot length is not as good as to practice a single foot-length. To practice a single foot-length is not as good as to leave it all behind."
"One inch. Why? The mountains are high and the waters are deep; the blue sky divides the bright sun. [The Master] lets out a shout.
[On the occasion of] visiting various mountains, he ascends the hall and cites the story of Master Lukmen. One day, a monk came to visit him. The monk asked:
"What is the family style of Lumen? The Master said, "There is salt and there is vinegar.
The monk asked, "What is it like for one on the Way? The Master said, "The mouth is like the nostrils. The monk asked, "If a guest should suddenly arrive, with what will you receive them?
The Master said, "A thatched gate and a grass door; thank you for passing by. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "Lumen’s family style is fully displayed; it is as impenetrable as water."

Since there was no intention to accept the jade tablet, how could there have been any intent to cede the city? Today, someone suddenly asks about the Golden Mountain: "What is the house style of the Golden Mountain?
To him, simply say: "Luminous and clear on all eight sides. "What is it like for one on the Way? "Directly out, directly in.
"If a guest should suddenly arrive, with what will you attend to them? "A pancake turns over upon the moon on the river; the sliced sashimi..."
"Clouds over the rooftops. Now tell me: how far apart are Jinshan’s words and those of Lukmon? Striking the whisk once, he said:
"When wine meets a true friend, it is drunk; when a poem meets one who understands, it is recited."
Xie Bingfu presides over the ritual for the *gānzhāi* (offering of food) and ascends the hall. Within the radiance of the jade mirror, the waves are clear and the moon appears.
He unfurls the hand that slays dragons and brandishes the Vajra sword; with a single squeeze, the thorny chestnuts and golden rings are opened. Let you chew them thoroughly and swallow them whole.

Having both illumination and function, both unfolding and rolling up—Yangqi’s news has not yet entirely vanished into ashes; the *udumbara* flower smiles upon the face of the spring breeze. *Zhuo!* (A striking gesture).
[He] strikes the staff once and gives a shout.
Ascending the hall on the first day of the year: Every year is a good year; every day is a good day. New Year people look upon Old Year people;
the days of the Old Year are the days of the New Year. The tide rises and reveals old marks; the tide falls and the stones appear. All things...
There is flux; yet flux is without change. There is change; yet it stands firm. [The Master] strikes his staff once and says: "Supreme good fortune!
Upon entering the hall for the Nirvana Sutra lecture, he said: "Old Śākyamuni plays with his own spirit; though dead, he remains as if he had never been so. He points to a tree.
The fallen flowers remain after spring has passed; the distant mountains stretch on, infinite layers of azure.
Entering the hall: The wind comes upon the river; the moon reaches the heart of the waves. Water and moon reflect each other’s light; the autumn sky is a single color.
Great men—whom among you does not possess a single *zuoju* (seating mat) of ground? Do you all attain correspondence with this? [He strikes the whisk.]
The Master struck the floor once and said: "In Wulin, spring has already faded; the terraces and pavilions are filled with lush green shade. He then ascended the hall and said:
"Perfection is identical to the great void—neither deficient nor excessive. It is only because of grasping and rejecting that one falls short.
The Great Master, the Third Patriarch, was much like lending a ladder to a thief; unaware, he brought harm upon his own life. Does Jìnshān have any way to transcend this?"
"Ma! [He] struck his staff once and said, "The donkey’s saddle bridge; it is not your father’s chin.
Ascending the hall to address the assembly amidst the snow, he said: "A night of river wind stirs the jade whisk; the solitary peak, no longer white, reveals its true spirit."
Letting go from emptiness, looking from emptiness—how many people have experienced this bone-chilling cold?
Ascending the hall for the retreat: North, South, East, West—how many paths? Coming and going, we share one small boat together.
Under the bright moon in the still night, amidst the Canglang River, A single pull of the line and a silvery fish follows the straight hook. Even so, is there anyone who does not swallow it?
"A hook baited with fragrant meat? He strikes the meditation staff once and says: "When both life and death are exhausted, the news is also exhausted;
even where there is no elegance, there is elegance.

[This was said] upon ascending the hall to thank the one who held the whisk and prepared the meal. Where wisdom does not reach, it is nonetheless possible to speak of it: swallow the long river dry and charge forward.
The azure void opens; the golden circle and the thorny plum are vividly present. Each heavenly flower is like creamy curd. The message of Yangqi remains intact;
before the mechanism of great function, it stands vividly alive. This mountain monk joins his palms, for he has his share; how shall you all chew and swallow?
Within the light of the jade mirror, the universe is vast; a pair of falcons from the distant heavens are released.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The height of the mountains and the depth of the waters are neither of the past nor of the present. The Old Barbarian lost a single sandal;
it cannot be found on the other side of the Pamir Mountains."

Ascending the hall: The wind howls with cold; the frost is piercingly sharp. The waves of the roof surge and crash, scattering silver and snow. Those who attempt to cross the current have not yet been called masters of the "Total Uplift.
To act as a physician for a dead horse is to let warmth meet warmth; with belly turned upside down and entrails poured out, a single thread passes through.
When the moon is bright, it does not borrow the whiteness of the reeds.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The long cannot emerge; the short cannot emerge. The four great oceans are not wide; the hole of a lotus fiber is not narrow.
It is beyond the reach of ears and eyes; it is beyond the scope of mind and intellect. From west to east, from south to north:
the setting clouds and the solitary wild goose fly together; the autumn waters and the vast sky share one color. He gave a shout and circled the hall.
Drinking Tea in the Hall.
Recorded sayings of the Chan Master of Baizhong Chan Temple in Luyuan, Tanzhou;
successor to the Dharma lineage of Lingyin Chan Temple in Hangzhou. Compiled by Jingfu.

The Master entered the temple and, pointing to the mountain gate, said, "This is where the Yellow-Faced Gautama first began to expound the Dharma, extensively delivering all sentient beings through the Great Gate of Expedient Means.
New Elder, with whom will you travel together to reach it? Zoubu replied, "I would take his hand and drag him in."

The Buddha Hall. The Buddha’s body is unconditioned and does not fall into any numerical categories. Why, then, is the merit of this single hall entirely composed of colored pigments and clay sculptures?
After a long silence, he said: "If there is no present, the ancient cannot be established."
Squatting in the chamber, he smelts Buddhas and refines patriarchs; he forges sages and melts ordinary beings. Life and death rest in his hands; the precious sword’s light is cold.
His intent lies in the stars, not upon the platter.

Ascending the seat, after the prayer for the Emperor has been concluded, he says: "The ancient mirror is without light, yet it reflects itself upon the dais; the myriad phenomena are devoid of shadow, yet none can escape being seen face-to-face."
He issued commands without speaking, and while seated, brought about Great Peace; he assisted in the transformation of non-action, until the six states were tranquil and clear.

Heaven is high and earth is deep; the waters are green and the mountains are blue. The mountains are blue and the waters are cool and clear; at the ancient ferry west of the Xiang River, the setting sun shines bright.
Mount Yue stands before the eaves like an unfolding painted screen.
Again, it is recounted: When Baoshou opened the hall for formal discourse, Sansheng brought forward a monk. Baoshou struck him immediately.
Sansheng said, "To act as a teacher in such a manner not only blinds this monk’s eyes, but blinds the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou.
Baoshou returned to his quarters. The Master [Zhaozhou] comments: This blow should have been eaten by Baoshou and Sansheng themselves. Why? Because everyone says: [it was the monk who was at fault].
These are the two sons of Linji; their righteousness brings forth a bountiful harvest. Yet they do not realize that it is precisely in times of scarcity that filial piety fails.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "The white peaches and the red apricots—the red apricots and the white peaches.

Whether rain or sun, whether cold or heat—each and every one is the place where you all cast off your bodies and surrender your lives. Why, then, do you refuse to accept this? Suddenly, there might be a man who comes forward..."
The Way. Elder, do you have no skillful means for others? Simply tell them: "The mouth is the gateway to calamity.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A long month has thirty days; a short month has twenty-nine. Suddenly spring ends and summer arrives;

one does not realize the night has come and sleeves are bared to the dew. Poor as having no silk to bind the ants, both within and without, all existence is empty. Hearing this, my staff leaps for joy."
He was filled with joy and said, "Caoshan once said to Master Shui, 'Qingyuan’s Bai Family served three cups of wine.
He then struck the ground once with his staff.
Ascending the hall. Striking the drum and ascending the hall, he speaks words of no meaning. If there were a single phrase that reached you all, your families and nations would flourish.
If there were not a single phrase that reached you all, the four seas would be peaceful and clear. He takes the pillar and places it upon the lantern;
he hangs the pillar by the side of the lantern. When hungry, one eats; when weary, one sleeps. What business is there? If...
"No. In the fifth month, the yellow plum stones will rot in the mortar.
He ascended the hall and said: "Before the Seven Buddhas and after Dīpaṃkara, no one could speak of it. Why, then, did [the Buddha] hold up a flower on Vulture Peak?"
Kāśyapa smiled. "In this land, those of talent and virtue are esteemed; in this family, the young children are cherished. When the Buddha ascended the hall for the Nirvana Sutra:
"Before the fifteenth day, there is existence today; after the fifteenth day, there will be non-existence tomorrow.
Precisely on the fifteenth day—is it existence? Is it non-existence? Stonehead said: "The large is large; the small is small."
Wild monkeys cry, shattering the dawn across a thousand mountains.
Entering the hall, he raised the teaching that says: "Far removed from inverted dreams and delusions, one reaches ultimate nirvana.
He cast aside the sweet peach tree and climbed the mountain to pluck sour pears. How many people can understand this news? If you do understand, it fills [the world].
Mountain flowers bloom and the cuckoo cries.
Recorded sayings of Shushan Baoyun Chan Monastery of Fuzhou;
compiled by Jingfu, Dharma Heir of Lingyin Chan Monastery in Hangzhou.
The Master entered the monastery and pointed to the mountain gate, saying: "The white clouds are high; the rapids flow swiftly. Without moving his feet, he enters the Buddha Hall with his whole body.
He continued: "The former Buddha left the city at midnight; the latter Buddha has not yet descended from the celestial palace. Now tell me, whom do you call..."
"That one acts as the Buddha of the present. (Inserting incense, he says: "Because of me, you receive my prostration.
(Taking up the memorial document: "Flowers cluster; brocade clusters. One cannot chant enough; one cannot sing enough. Truly, it is the melody upon the stringless lute."
Ascending the seat, he offered incense and made his vow for the Emperor, then said:
"The great capacity responds perfectly; the great wisdom is without fixed direction. Meeting the source on either side, there are openings through every hole."
Ten thousand layers of clouded mountains pass away in a single stroke; at the head of the Eighteen Rapids, the sound roars on. When encountering the noble, one is noble;

Xie Bingfu then went back to the abbot's quarters and said, "The Master said I lacked the eye of the ancients. Fayan said, "What eye do you have? Bingfu held up the fan. Fayan said, "Is that the eye? Bingfu threw the fan down and left. Fayan said, "This fellow has a bit of spirit, but he still lacks the eye of the ancients. Xie Bingfu then went back to the abbot's quarters and said, "
"The fan is already broken; give me back my rhinoceros! How about that? He strikes the meditation staff once and says:
"The horns and head are already fully revealed; one sight is worth a thousand hearings."
Ascending the hall on the Double Ninth: There is one phrase, most elegant and refined; it truly surpasses gold. It lies right beneath the eastern fence.
If you see it, see it at once—avoid all hesitation! Whether it is so or not depends entirely on your choosing and rejecting. For now, do not be caught up in such deliberations.
A letter arrived from the Elder Fuchu of Shishuang Huayan, a successor in the Dharma lineage. He ascended the hall and said: "The monkey cries in the withered tree;
the tiger roars at the precipice. A single lamp flares up, and the myriad phenomena are viewed as one. As for this staff, it cannot help but dance with the hands and leap with the feet.
He struck the staff once and asked: "Why is this? The World-Honored One had no secret words; Kāśyapa did not break his smile."
On the Buddha’s Birthday, he ascended the hall. He took seven steps and walked all around; nine dragons bathed him.

Bare and naked, who would say his body was not fully endowed with both merit and wisdom? Shaoyang beats him to death, yet it is truly something to boast of: a severed string can always be mended by phoenix glue.
The Buddha ascends the hall after attaining the Way. Before Mount Zhengjue, when the morning star was bright and clear, he lost his nostrils at midnight.
One might think that with this, everything was finally settled; yet Zhongzhu observes that there is still a deficiency here—it would have been better not to speak of it.
When the eyes open, the sky is already wide awake.

Upon receiving the news of his Preceptor’s passing, he ascended the hall and said: "From the very beginning, you were already born into the wrong womb; you have been deceived by these ghostly faces and divine heads.
You have rent asunder the void, leaving not a single crack or seam. Raising his whisk, he said: "The whisk of tortoise hair performs the Three Platforms dance!"
Taking leave of the assembly, he proceeded to Lingyin Monastery. Ascending the hall, he said: "With hair white and hanging down, an old man who has long been possessed by demons;
Wandering among those of different species, his transgressions are many. Since the karmic debts are deep, they remain unpaid; He must once again drag a plow through the misty thickets."
Record of the Sayings at Lingyin Jingde Chan Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture.
Compiled by Jìngfú, Dharma Heir of the Chan Monastery of Lingyin in Hangzhou.
When the Master entered the monastery, he pointed to the mountain gate and said: "The ultimate barrier above—throughout the entire world, there is no door for people to enter. New...
Lingyin: Today, with the eight characters wide open, I invite everyone to enter from here.
In the Buddha Hall: Deshan would tear it down; Yunmen would beat it to death. When the true command is fully raised, there is no one to oppose it. Spreading his sitting mat, he said:
"The net that covers the heavens is gathered all at once."
Seated in his quarters, he took up his staff and said: "If it comes from the bright side, strike it on the bright side; if it comes from the dark side, strike it on the dark side.
But what if it does not come in either way? How then? He leaned the staff against [the wall] and rose.

Holding up the imperial edict and the official decree: this is the life-vein of the patch-robed monks and the eye of the Buddhas and patriarchs; it does not require even a single decree. But tell me, as for the matter beyond this, what then?
After a long silence, he said: "The Imperial Decree has been issued; the six kingdoms have long been known to be purified."
Regarding the Dharma seat: when one wishes to ascend this seat, one must first pay homage to the Tathāgata Sumerudīparāja. At the new Lingyin Monastery, it is not so;
for wherever there is a path that can be ascended, those who are superior in spirit will also travel upon it.

Ascending the seat, after the prayer for the Emperor has been concluded, he says: "At Vulture Peak, when the flower was held up, the hundreds of thousands of devas and humans shared in the opportunity to gaze upon it. At Shaolin, the direct pointing..."
Two, three, four, seven. Seeking out the traces and origins, one thoroughly clarifies the true eye of Maheśvara and brings forth the sublime mechanism of the Ultimate.
It fills the ten voids; not even a speck of dust can be established. At this very moment, what is the phrase for opening the hall and offering prayers for the Emperor?
The mind is like the waters of the Qiantang River: Silent, it flows toward the east day after day.
Again, he raised an example. Emperor Taizong, while a monk was paying his respects at court, addressed him, saying, "Your Majesty, do you still remember this humble monk?
The Emperor asked, "Where did we meet? The monk replied, "We parted at Vulture Peak, and it has been until this very day.

The Emperor asked, "What proof is there of this? The monk was speechless. The Master said: "This humble monk, Pudu, finds such a rare opportunity difficult to encounter; I shall therefore offer a verse. He then recited it.
Resembling a great assembly, his virtue harmonizes with heaven and earth as he governs the nine heavens. Auspicious light and auspicious qi shroud the mountains and rivers.
In the moment when the teaching is fully presented face-to-face, the assembly on Vulture Peak is once again solemnly present.

That evening’s informal discourse: Opening wide the doors and windows, a single breath of harmony—the springtime of Shaolin. Sitting grandly facing the window, the three-foot cold light is the command of Mahākāla.
The Dharma follows the practice of the Dharma; the banner of the Dharma is erected wherever it may be. He carelessly hurls the thorny chestnut.
He hurls a golden ring upward; ancient and modern merge, and the paths of sage and ordinary are cut off. Nevertheless, he strikes the meditation staff once and says:
"Only when one returns to the Great Kingdom is one truly noble; only when water reaches the vast ocean does it become a true wave."
Again, Master Fadingeng said: "This mountain monk originally intended to hide deeply within a mountain cave to cultivate the Way until my time had passed.
However, because my late master has a case that remains unresolved, I have come forth to settle it for him. At that time, a monk asked:
"How is it that this is the unresolved public case of our former master? Dēng took up his staff and struck, saying, "The patriarch failed to resolve it;
the calamity reaches the descendants. The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie? Dēng said, "The fault lies with you; the calamity reaches me.
The Master said, "I too wished to hide deep in mountain caves to cultivate the Way until my time passed, but I could not bear it, for the venerable teacher Sōnyen had—"
Thus, this unresolved koan has brought misfortune upon the former master, passing down through the generations until today.
Do you all wish to recognize this unresolved koan of the venerable master Songyuan? It is late at night and I have stood for long.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "When a false person preaches the True Dharma, the True Dharma is entirely false. When a true person preaches false dharma, the false dharma is entirely true.
He struck the meditation staff once. "False? True? He struck the meditation staff once again. "Preaching? Not preaching?
If you can discern and distinguish this point, then even a house made of gold is not considered noble; jade food and brocade robes are likewise of no account.
What is there to be truly honored? He ascended the hall and said: "The Stone of Dhūta is enveloped in moss; Peak of Thrown Pens is entangled with *bìlì* vines.
In the Hall of Arhats, three novices are ordained each year; in Guizong Monastery, one drinks tea after the formal session. How excellent, all you practitioners of Zen! Truly."
Master Jing was a native of Guansi. He was accustomed to handling large banners and drums;
why, then, upon arriving here, did he not dare to move even a single thread? (The Master) strikes his staff once: "You must believe that the source flows from ten-thousand-fathom heights;
a single line breaks through the color of the green mountains."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are but the clarity of the nature. Originally there is no person who is deluded or awakened; it simply requires that you be resolved today.
Since there is no person who is deluded or awakened, what is there to be resolved? He struck the meditation staff once and said: "A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them;
they are merely followed by the warbling oriole over the low wall."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The mind-king does not move falsely; the six realms are simultaneously penetrated. Lay aside the three-foot sword; cease playing with the single bow.
To present it in such a manner is to provide a ladder for a thief.
Do you all wish to see Master Huanglong? 'Sweeping away stones to sit, the sleeves of the robe grow cold; treading upon flowers returning home, the horse's hooves are fragrant.'"
Ascending the hall, he raised the example of Master Yunmen addressing the assembly, saying: "All of you here passing the summer retreat—this mountain monk truly does not wish to speak to you.
Just cherish your eyebrows! The Master commented: "Master Yunmen was like a sacred tortoise dragging its tail;
as it wiped away its tracks, the tracks multiplied. Lingyin is not so. All of you here passing the summer retreat—"
I speak these direct words of the Sangha to you: the mouth is the gateway to calamity.
[He] ascended the hall and raised the example of Huanglong Caotang Heshang, who addressed the assembly, saying: "Those of the highest capacity awaken to a thousand things upon hearing them once."

One attains the Great Dhāraṇī. Yet for those of middling-middle capacity, whose families are poor and find it difficult to provide vegetarian food, one must rely on verbal explanations to manifest the Way.
When pressed by affairs and unable to write in cursive script, those of the lowest-lower capacity cling to words as fixed principles, remaining stuck in their shells and lost in delusive confinement.
A fine hawk does not strike at sparrows by the fence. Huanglong Wushan weighed and measured with scales and bushels; there was not a hair’s breadth of error.
Lingyin, however, is like one who sells flour mixed with bran, unable to distinguish between beans and wheat. Even so, who knows which of them is without calculation?
Upon tasting it, cold sweat flows over one's entire body.
Addressing Elder Heshan and the Head Cook, the Master ascends the hall: "Extinguishing the Eye of the True Dharma, wearing the seal of Vairocana, he wields the adze;

every beat of the hand is the command. At the head of the White Water fields, deep within the small stream, the Good Knowledge of fifteen hundred men draws from the tip of his ladle—head straight, tail straight.
Salt is salty, vinegar is bland; the livelihood is already perfected. *Jin* (Pound).
Both are self-settled. Do you all know where they fall? (He strikes the meditation staff once. When the object meets the master, the eye stands upright.
After thanking the supervisor for collecting [the staff], he ascends the hall. The life-vein of the patch-robed monk—(he strikes the meditation staff once)—is all here. There is letting go.
There is one who gathers it in; entering the mud, entering the water, he holds it firmly and maintains mastery. A ten-thousand-bushel pearl, returning in triumph.
Carrying his sword, he simply goes off to sleep.
The letter from the late Master Wudeng of Daochang arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "The tiger beneath Tiger Rock—its fangs do not show when it bites.
It crouches and sits, majestic and imposing; there is no path north or south. With a single somersault, it casts itself away, leaving no trace.
Empty space claps its hands and Mount Sumeru dances. The myriad phenomena and the forest of forms all suffer at once; the stone man and the wooden man weep like rain."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Zen Master Linji, who said: "There is one person who, for kalpas, remains on the road yet never leaves home;
there is another person who leaves home yet is not on the road. Which of these two is worthy of receiving the offerings of devas and humans?

The Master commented: "Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have no horns. An inch of hair and a centimeter of silk—the heavens and earth are vast and empty. [At this point,] Pan Lang fell over backward.
Riding a donkey. He falls and kills the yellow barbarian as he leaps away.
Entering the hall: Before the fifteenth day, it is a silver mountain and an iron wall; after the fifteenth day, it is an iron wall and a silver mountain.
It is precisely on the fifteenth day. Not a single speck of dust remains; heaven and earth are vast and wide. Who would have known there was yet another barrier beyond?
(He strikes the meditation staff once. Entering the hall:
Within the gate of the Patriarchs, what need is there to seek any "handle"? Going east or going west, there is neither right nor wrong. Suddenly—
The chrysanthemums beneath the hedge are yellow; at this time, it is certainly the Double Ninth Festival.
[The Master] closes the stove and ascends the hall. "At the head of the fire-stove there is a single phrase. If you can utter it completely, I dare not grant you my approval.
Lingyin does not suppress the worthy to elevate the lowly. [He] strikes the meditation staff once. "If an object sees its master, both eyes stand wide open."
The Buddha ascended the path to enlightenment. At midnight, he leaped over the city wall. A man of light does not perform dark deeds. For six years he suffered from cold and hunger;
what he did himself, he must now return to himself and receive the consequences. But when he beheld the morning star, what did he realize? It is difficult to deceive the eyes of the multitude.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Where the Buddhas have not reached in their practice, take one step forward.

Where the Buddhas have not spoken, utter a single phrase. Even if you were to reach both in practice and speech, you would still deserve a blow from my staff. Why? Because seeking fire, you have obtained it along with the smoke."
Carrying the spring and wearing the moon, he returns.
Ascending the hall, he held up his whisk and said: "This very thing is it. To look toward Yuzhou from ten thousand miles away, one must not seek elsewhere apart from this."
Standing on the precipice, one gazes upon the banks: peach blossoms red, pear blossoms white; waters green, mountains blue. Neither borrowed nor not borrowed—every dharma is fundamentally thus.
But what of it when the position is shifted and the mechanism is turned? The night moon does not follow the flowing water;
a single cloud mostly returns to its old mountain.
Ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat: A single knot on the head of the布袋 (Fotu) bag; the news from the hundred cities is cut off.
Is the wax figure cold or not? Ten thousand miles, a single line of iron. Coral branches, branch upon branch, support the moon.
Ascending the hall: For this ninety-day session, it is an iron wall, and yet another iron wall. From the four quarters and eight directions they come, yet none can leap out.
The setting clouds fly side by side with the solitary wild goose; the autumn waters share the same hue as the vast sky.

On the fifteenth day of the fifth month, he went out on a journey. Ascending the hall, he said: "Short oars and light sails; the wind is calm and the waves are still. The lake's radiance overflows the eyes, as level as a mirror.

Before the fishermen’s songs have begun, with whom can one listen? Ten thousand valleys and a thousand crags respond universally to the heights and depths, amidst the scattered remnants of sunset clouds.
As the prow turns, everything is gathered in. At such a time as this, what is it? He struck his staff.
One day he said: "In the kingdom of Muktika, [the king] personally issued this decree.
He ascended the hall and said: "From the time of the ancient ancestors until now, there has been a direct and authentic transmission. With teeth clenched tight, it is not to be leaked like water.
Among those who appear in groups of three or two, some possess the strategy to sweep away the Three Qin; yet they disdain even to be Buddhas. If you reach the gate of Lingyin..."
"Down! Furthermore, how could you possibly avoid thirty blows?
Thank you, Master Xuefeng Jue'an, for ascending the hall. With the sacred talisman in hand, the Great Function is fully manifested. Where the wooden ball rolls, thunder shakes and the wind blows.
When the 'tortoise-nose' is seized, it is tossed crosswise and cast upward; demons and heretics retreat in awe at the precipice, while the Buddhas..."
The Patriarch peers about, yet finds no door; he sits, cutting off the vital ford. When the ten directions are thus thoroughly open and unobstructed—at such a time as this, tell me:
what is the phrase that takes up the hand? We meet and there is nothing more to do; if you do not come, I shall still think of you.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The sun may grow cold; the moon may grow hot. No demons can destroy the True Teaching. But tell me, what is the True Teaching?
It is the cycle of formation, abiding, destruction, and emptiness."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: King Kaniṣka of Jibin deeply revered the Triple Gem.
One day, brandishing his sword, he asked the Venerable Siṃha, "Have you attained the emptiness of the aggregates? The Venerable replied, "I have attained the emptiness of the aggregates.

The King said, "Have you escaped birth and death? The Venerable replied, "I have escaped birth and death. The King said, "Since you have escaped birth and death, you may give me your head. The Venerable replied, "My body..."
"It does not belong to me; why begrudge my head? The King then beheaded him. The Master said, "A masterful Kapiśa King.
From the Venerable One’s head, white milk surged forth several feet high. The Master said, "An adept presenting his skill to an adept. [The King then severed] his left arm.
Immediately, [the head] fell to the ground. The Master said, "I received an ox from one man; I return a horse to another. Everyone, tell me:
was this King of Kaśmīra repaying kindness and returning virtue to the Venerable Siṃha? Or was it the suffering of meeting with an enemy?

If you can discern the black and the white here, then throughout the twelve periods of the day, your efforts will not be in vain. If this is not yet so, [then... (Note: The final character "數" appears to be an incomplete or corrupted fragment of the text.)
The sound of the Qiang flute lingers at the parting pavilion at evening; you head toward Xiao and Xiang, while I head toward Qin.
Ascending the hall: On the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month, Dongshan departed from Chadu. "Alas, old Yunmen! He has added one more final phrase.
When the peach-blossom waves warm and the Yu Gate rises high, with a single stroke of thunder, he burns his tail and departs.
The Buddha ascends the hall after attaining the Way: "Old Gautama’s eye-sockets are too small; they cannot contain even a whole star or half a star.

When will your talk of delusion and enlightenment ever end? Within the domain of a patch-robed monk, how many such varieties can there be? The snow has cleared, the sea is vast, and the thousand peaks are bright at dawn."
Ascending the hall: When Bodhidharma came from the West, he knew only this one thing: the iron wall and silver mountain—no matter how much one prods them, they cannot be penetrated.
Why, then, did he speak of "dividing the skin" and "dividing the marrow"? The Feilai Peak is high; the Lingquan Spring is green.
When Baizhang Wuhui sent off a monkey, he ascended the hall and said: "A monk once asked Baizhang, 'What is the extraordinary matter?

Baizhang replied, 'Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak. The Master then offered this verse: Majestically sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak, Ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains stand below his wind.
Though they meet, they do not speak of extraordinary matters; A single cry of a monkey resounds amidst the green mists.
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival: No peach talismans are nailed; no mugwort tigers are hung. Harnessing the mechanism of the iron ox, he beats the poison-dripping drum.
A thousand demons and a hundred monsters all hide their traces; atop Vulture Peak, the sun stands high at noon.
Master Yunfeng ascended the hall at Jiangshan. Leaning his staff upon his shoulder, he said: "The Master Bao is coming!
Upon the tip of this staff, there is an inch-long and a foot-short; its trimming and sweeping are distinct. Thus it goes, descending the mountain to transform sentient beings.
Entering the mud and entering the water, he blocks off the vital pass; tiger-pacing and dragon-coiling—within this, there is one who does not accept appraisal."
It is beyond measure; it cannot be removed by clipping or brushing away. Furthermore, how can it be dispelled? [The Master] strikes the meditation staff once and says:
"Let loose the moon atop Mount Zhongfu; it shall see off the man treading the reeds as he crosses the river."

Ascending the hall, Xuedou said: "A straight hook catches the *kūn* and the *jīng*; a curved hook catches turtles and turtles. If a curved hook were used for the *kūn* and *jīng*, it would logically be unsuitable;

if a straight hook were used for turtles and turtles, their feelings would likewise be dissatisfied. To distinguish dragons from snakes and capture tigers and rhinoceroses, one must rely on the old man Xuedou.
But as for wanting to catch both *kūn* and *jīng* along with turtles and turtles—I dare not grant permission. Lingyin’s Hook.
There is no bending or straightening; whether it be a *kūn* or *jīng*, a tortoise or a turtle, one asks nothing of them all. Why? "The fishing rod is worn away, so plant bamboo anew;
do not calculate the labor, but rest when you have caught it."
The Venerable Benjue Xushimian arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "The great capacity responds perfectly; the great function has no fixed direction.
Shattering the broken sand-pot, he extinguishes the Eye of the True Dharma. Holding fast at the vital ford, Buddhas and Patriarchs hide their traces. From the main case, he brings up the side."
Hitting the mark every hundred times—just go like this. But tell me, whose moon and wind is this? Before the Zhuli Pavilion, the *moke* command;
the whole sky is filled with harmonious breath, the spring of Shaolin.
Ascending the hall: In the eighth and ninth months, it is neither cold nor hot. Panshan cast his sword into the void; this is precisely such a season.
Without past or present, without interval or cessation. When the clouds of delusion have rolled away and the sound of rain has ceased, ten thousand miles stretch as a single blade of iron.

Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Elder Master Baiyun Shouduan addressed the assembly, saying, "If you can truly achieve a single instance of breaking into a sweat, you will manifest a palace of jade and crystal upon a single blade of grass.
If you have not achieved a single instance of breaking into a sweat, then even if there were a palace of jade and crystal, it would be covered over by a single blade of grass.
The Master commented: "Elder Master Baiyun, out of his great compassion..."
These are words from the weeds. Under the gate of Lingyin, whether you are upright or not, even if there were towers of jade and palaces of crystal, there would be no place for them to rest.
You all, tell me: is this a sentence of clarified butter (*tīrtha*)? Is it a sentence of poison?
"How many times have I seen you and inquired deeply? The intention to raise chickens lies in the fifth watch."
The Double Ninth. Also, expressing gratitude for the Dharma Hall discourse by Master Zhiti. Dewdrops fall; the wind is piercing.

Chrysanthemum fragrance fills the path—why should it be found only at the eastern hedge? Responding universally to high and low, it accompanies one at every step. Sometimes upon the banks of the Zhu Jing River.
A fine silken thread hangs lightly; the prow of the boat turns. The celestial crown has always been at the caitya—why? Because when encountering strength, one yields weakness.
An old friend arrives. Entering the hall: Fallen leaves drift; the autumn river is clear and shallow. When heroes meet, the halberds and spears are not unfurled—why?
Because words, once spoken, distance one further from the Way.
Ascending the hall for the opening of the furnace: The color of cold pervades all under heaven; the great earth serves as the furnace.

One sees only the clear wind standing like a wall, unaware that the stones are crumbling and the pines are withered. Why did the Hall Master lose his eyebrows and beard when Danxia burned the wooden Buddha?
[The Master] strikes the staff once: Without this spark of fire, how could one seek out the old bearded barbarian from the West?
A letter from the late Master Zu’eng of Jiaoshan arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "The sea gates have been turbulent with waves all night;
the Jade Unicorn has broken its golden horn. Fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs have all hidden their traces; even the thousand hands of Mahākaruṇika cannot find them.
The wooden horse neighs in sorrow, and the stone man sheds tears. Tell me, everyone: was Master Zu’eng alive or dead? [He remained silent for a long time.]
Ting-tuo carried a cloth bag; Puhua shook his bells.
Entering the hall, he said: "Rest! Cease! A single thought for ten thousand years! A single length of white silk! An incense burner in an ancient temple! He gave a shout and said:
"If you do not find flowing water, you must still pass over other mountains."

A letter from the late Venerable Xutang of Mount Jing arrived; he ascended the hall and said: "The Peak that Pierces the Heavens rises abruptly from the earth, towering and majestic against the vast void.
One night, a celestial wind suddenly snapped it down. The wooden horse neighs in sorrow; the stone man chokes with grief. At dawn, the clouds disperse and the valley breeze clears;
for a thousand ages, Xutang’s empty hall reflects the bright moon."
On the anniversary of Master Wude’s passing, he held up the incense and said: "The rolling, bottomless surges of East Lake; the sky-scraping thorns of the green mountains.
Meeting on these two narrow paths, he is pressed until he climbs the wall. Enmity is hard to repay, gratitude is hard to repay.
Hot-boiled cold spring water flows; a single bowl of lightly tinted tea."

He leaves two groups of monks to ascend the hall. Planting his staff on the dais, he says: "There is the provisional and the real; there is the illuminating and the functioning. These are but the eyes of ghosts;

they must be handled with life at the moment of opportunity. When handled with life, there is no distinction between the distant and the near. Who would have known that beneath these scholar’s caps are all but people from times past?"
The Head Seat, Xie, held the whisk; the Abbot of the Monastery provided the meal. Ascending the hall, he said: "The single phrase prior to sound shifts the constellations like turning over a bowl.

The spark of flint cannot reach it; the flash of lightning cannot pursue it. A thorn from a chestnut tree is hurled right before one's face; a sword of absolute steel is wielded with the hand of confidence.
He struck his staff once and said: "The news of Shaolin is cut off; the flower blooms on a branch that has never sprouted."
At the Yongcou Middle Elder’s Hall at Wanshou Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture; the Meiyang Mo Elder at Guangfu; and the Nanshe Yue Elder at Yuelin, appearing in this world.
Ascending the hall, he said: "One is three; three is one. Bodhidharma never left Shaoshi Mountain.
Though father and son are close, the wondrous truth is not transmitted. The single flower and five petals have become a tangled mess. The sea wind blows up a rage."
The waves are cold; those who cross the current do not get their feet wet. The Way lies in the Middle Way. The plum fragrance on the rocky crags;
the broken sandpot rings with a clear chime. It depends on you to skillfully cast it away.
[With the whisk, he draws a circle and strikes once more. Do you all know where it lands? If you do not yet know, wait until the future to ask.
Maitreya, on the Dragon Boat Festival, I ascend the hall. Although Mañjuśrī commanded Sudhana to gather medicinal herbs, he has never once cured the Buddha’s illness or the Patriarchs’ illness.
At Lingyin, there is neither illness nor medicine. Zhaozhou hangs a gourd from the eastern wall.
The Buddha’s Birthday: Ascending the Hall. Two thousand years ago, within the Lumbinī Garden, the earth shook and the mountains trembled as a calamitous source suddenly arose.
Yunmen’s blind staff could not kill him; the descendants of later generations merely gnash their teeth in vain. Do not gnash your teeth!
Whether the handle of the ladle is long or short, it is up to you to pour it out.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "To speak of Chan and to speak of the Way is easy; to become a Buddha and become a Patriarch is difficult. When the Great Mountain in front of the gate suddenly emerges, becoming a Buddha and becoming a Patriarch is easy;
to speak of Chan and to speak of the Way is difficult. A Persian from the South Sea recites the 'Eight Returns'—this is neither difficult nor easy.
Where a patch-robed monk strikes, his nose reaches the vast heavens. He struck the meditation staff once and asked: "What is this place?"
While speaking of what is difficult and what is easy, he again struck his staff once and said: "In official matters, even a needle cannot pass;
in private affairs, carriages and horses may go through. He then ascended the hall and said: "The teachings state that Subhūti asked Śāriputra, 'What constitutes the Buddha-eye? Śāriputra replied:"
"Taking intrinsic emptiness as the Buddha-eye. Subhūti said, "Excellent, excellent! All the Buddhas of the past have likewise taken intrinsic emptiness as the Buddha-eye.
The Master picked it up and said, "Sewn with needles and joined with glue, not a single drop leaks through. But tell me, everyone:
ultimately, what constitutes the Buddha-eye? He let out a shout.
A letter from the late Master Yuan-sou of Wanshou Monastery in Pingjiang arrived; [the Master] ascended the hall and said:

"Last night, the Vairambha wind shook the mountains and peaks; seventy-two summits all toppled over. Ten thousand acres of Lake Tai were not a single drop of water; yellow leaves fell in disorder as the stars and constellations descended.
Do you wish to see Master Yuan-sou? The jade hare pushes open the Eight-Eulogy Tower; the golden crow pecks through the crystal."

Liguo. Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: A monk asked Fayan, "When the autumn wind first stirs, upon what does the poor man rely? Fayan said, "If you can recognize kindness, only then will you know how to repay it.
The Master said, "This monk is clutching his stolen goods while crying out for injustice; Fayan, though, knows the thief but fails to apprehend him. Although...
However, out of the compassion of the Dharma-eye, there are words that descend into the weeds; alas, those who truly understand them are few.
Lingyin has thus raised this song—does anyone here understand? After a long silence, he said: "Yellow leaves flutter, filling the courtyard."
A single sound of the mortar and pestle falls in whose house?
At Shuanglin in Wuzhou, ascending the hall: To open the mouth is not Chan; to close the mouth is not the Way.
It is simply this wheel-pestle; when picked up and used, it is perfectly suited. One strike and the Celestial Gate opens; the myriad phenomena all collapse together. Narrow!
Meeting suddenly on the road, they clap their hands and laugh "he-he. But tell me, what are they laughing at? Meeting brings no matter;
when you do not come, I still remember you.
In the Snow. A thank-you to the various granaries, treasuries, and supervisors. Ascending the hall: Entering the wasteland, emerging from the wasteland;
grasping at will, every grain is perfectly round. Horizontally three thousand, vertically three thousand. Though it is called "empty flowers before the eyes," it is in truth clear and transparent.
Within the realm of the patch-robed monk, there is releasing and gathering, there is opening and closing. How so? A single spark on a red-hot furnace.

Dianxue. A formal address upon ascending the hall to thank the elders of the three monasteries on the high terrace of Nantai. Yantou Xueqiao and Qingshan shared the same track and traveled the same path;
how could this be considered ordinary? To recognize the true white-marked tiger of Nantai, one must know that his body has always been identical to that of a tiger.
Bān: "Just go like this. When the assembly of a million followers at Vulture Peak was thus [awakened], how could it have been limited to the breaking of a smile by the Golden Ascetic alone?
At that moment, the Eye of the True Dharma was extinguished; holding hands and walking alone, heaven and earth were vast.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient precedent. A monk once asked an ancient worthy, "What is one who practices great cultivation?
The worthy replied, "Carrying a cangue and wearing shackles. The monk asked again, "What is one who performs great work? The worthy replied, "Practicing dhyāna and cultivating samādhi.
The Master said, "The words of this ancient worthy resonate with truth; within his phrases he conceals a subtle mechanism. He was like a skilled archer whose arrows never miss their mark. Moreover—"
The Way. Is there still a path for emerging from it? A sweet melon is sweet down to its stem; a bitter gourd is bitter to its very root.
When Master Shilou went to Wanshou in Pingjiang, he ascended the hall and said: "Miaoxi’s black bamboo cane—does it have a back, or does it have a front?
If one's descendants can use it intimately, their whole body will be eyes. When the true command is fully raised, it turns smoothly like a waterwheel. Flowers cluster..."
A dense cluster of brocade; it would cause even the Buddhas and Patriarchs to lower their heads. Since the universe has been empty, who else could there be?
The Buddha ascends the hall at Nirvāṇa: "In the city of Kuśinagara there is birth and death; in this world of mine, there is no birth or death.
When the peach blooms red and the plum blooms white, the mountains and rivers everywhere unfold like a painted scroll. Śākyamuni the Old Man was naturally thus hidden.
The body has no path. Why say so? "Tonight he enters parinirvāṇa. Alas! Alas!
To what mountain did Master Jue’an go? Entering the hall, he said: "Using the adze—neither heavy nor light; picking it up or putting it down, the talisman behind the elbow is efficacious.
It reaches such a state that the clouds are layered upon one another, the waters of the Xia River ripple, and the small stream spreads across the heavens."
An iron net catches the living golden-scaled fish. Ultimately, what serves as the basis? "The opening of the mouth does not reside on the tongue. Ascending the hall:
Before Qingming and after Hanshi, flower-rain fills the heavens and clouds cover the peaks. Whose young calf has its strength not yet perfected?
It knows only to follow the herd and run in the pack. A-he-he! The rope’s head remains in the old man’s hand. When...
When the trigger is pulled and severed in a single stroke, the wild jackal immediately lets out a lion’s roar. Although this is so, those who recognize gratitude are few.
Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "If you come by boat, you arrive; if you come by land, you arrive. Whether by boat or by land, the red sun shines brightly amidst the white clouds."
The scarred hollows are blue; spring is in Shaolin and has never aged. Now tell me: is there anything further above this?
Treading upon it, one does not become angry.

Ascending the hall: Ten days have passed since the summer retreat began, yet there is no news of that matter. Clouds rest idly upon the mountain peaks; why does the water flow so urgently? Not a single dharma is concealed;
from ancient times to the present, there has been no trace. Have you not seen what Panshan said? "It is like throwing a sword into the air:
do not even discuss whether one reaches it or not. After a long silence, he said: "In a single day, the alms bowl becomes wet twice."
Ascending the hall: The rice seedlings have entered the soil; the wheat has been brought to the threshing floor. A bountiful year is already foretold; every house is filled with granaries.
When hunger comes, one eats; when heat comes, one seeks coolness. Tumbling eastward and staggering westward, one follows conditions as they arise. There is nothing further to deliberate upon.
Last night, however, I was startled by the cry of the cuckoo. Why does it break the heart so? It is because the Old Man Yama demands the price for his meal.

[The Master] requests the Supervisor to ascend the hall. He cites the Fifth Patriarch’s words: "Four or five hundred *shí* of wheat, two or three thousand *chèng* of rice—what an excellent recipe for abstaining from grain!
Even Jīvaka could not have devised such a wonder. The Master comments: "How extraordinary, the old fellow, the Fifth Patriarch!"
Proclaimed from within the midst of non-existence, it is fully encompassed within the realm of existence. All at once, it is cast before the faces of all people;
yet, for what reason, can it not be chewed through? It is because there are hungry people sitting right beside a basket of rice.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To see that the body has no reality is the Buddha’s vision; to realize that the mind is like an illusion is the Buddha’s realization.

When one realizes that the fundamental nature of body and mind is empty, how does such a person differ from the Buddha? Those who sit, sit; those who stand, stand. At every turn and in every encounter, [this is so]."
"It is not some other thing. After all, which one is the Buddha? After a long silence, he said: "The rustic elder knows nothing of the labors of Yao and Shun;
drum beats roll as they sacrifice to the River God."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Pressed, one immediately moves; citing one to clarify three. To gauge the mechanism and weigh the measure is like gazing at Mount Penglai from across the sea—three myriad *li* away over the Weak Waters.
"Among you in the assembly, have you heard such words and felt your ears prick up in sudden realization, or found them unsatisfying?
Come forward and discuss it. If not, then in this new autumn, rain falls from a thousand homes behind the curtains."
On this day, a single flute sounds atop the pavilions in the breeze.

On the occasion of the Longevity Festival, I ascend the hall. When one Buddha appears in the world, auspicious light spreads across the earth; in a single thought, ten thousand years pass, and the Mountain of Longevity grows ever more verdant.
At dawn the wind rises and fills the courtyard with fragrance, blowing open three or five blossoms upon the coiled peach tree.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "This Dharma abides in its own station; the characteristics of the world are eternally constant. Yesterday there was a great wind and tide that blew down the trees before the mountain.
The clouds fly toward the heavens; the waters flow toward the sea. These are still merely the characteristics of the world.
How can one speak of that which is eternally constant? He struck the meditation staff. "A thousand emptinesses do not equal a single reality."

Retired Master Tenggeng entered the Patriarchs’ Hall. Employing both gentle and fierce fires, he wielded the hammer and tongs of severity to crush the thieving minds of dead scholars and open the eyes and ears of humanity.
Before his great function, the wheel turns with effortless ease; he is ten parts compassion and ten parts deadly venom.
Sixth, he dwelt at the famous monastery and returned with a smile. Under the cold light of the blue lamp at night, the fragrance of incense wafted richly.
Regarding the encroachment upon the grounds in front of the mountain by Jiqing Temple, a provincial decree was received to restore them. He ascended the hall and said:
"A single expanse of idle land before the mountain, For vast kalpas it has had no boundaries. Today it is reclaimed and returned; He sits firmly, cutting off all tracks."
Head and tail joined; the east is so, the west is so—north, south, east, and west are not otherwise.
Ultimately, how does one repay such kindness and virtue? A single stick of incense before the Hall of Direct Pointing; ten *li* of lotus flowers, nine *li* of pines.
Compiled by Jingfu, Dharma Heir of the Chan Temple of Lingyin in Hangzhou, formerly Abbot of Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Temple in Jingshan, Lin’an Prefecture.

As the Master entered the temple, he held up the ceremonial document (*zhai*) and said: "The eye of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, the life-vein of heaven and humanity—everything is contained herein. All you people..."
If you have sufficient faith, do not hesitate to lend an ear.
Taking up the monastery’s introductory discourse: there is gold within the house and scales outside; whether the salt is salty or the vinegar is bland, the weight is determined of its own accord.
Spontaneously, one encounters the source at every turn; it can be taken for granted that every beat is the true command.

Taking up the "Announcement to the Rivers and Lakes," people forget one another in the Way and its arts; fish forget one another in the rivers and lakes. Since they are said to have forgotten one another—
Holding up the commentary, he said: "What is the use of needing this?
As for the Dharma seat—when the ancients said, 'This seat is so high and vast that I cannot ascend it,' what kind of words were those?
When one's strength is exhausted, the mountain is all the more beautiful."
Ascending the seat, he offered incense to pray for the Emperor.
Having finished, he next held up the incense and said: "This one portion of incense has been offered eight times over thirty years;
let us now behold its final, most earnest offering. It is dedicated to my late teacher, who formerly resided at Huazang Chan Temple in Baizhong County, Changzhou."
[The Master] burned incense in the burner to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk of his late teacher, Wude Heshang. He sat cross-legged and said: "The doors and windows are flung wide open;
ten thousand mountains push through the lattice, sending their greenery in. "Sitting grandly facing the courtyard, not a bird comes; the spring day is long."
Responding universally to high and low, sound and form are entirely true. Grasping the firm barrier, not even a drop of water can leak through.

The wind of Yao is vast and sweeping; the sun of Shun is bright and joyful. Not involving sight or hearing, one hits the mark every hundred times. After all, whose grace and power does this rely upon? The green mountains do not lock in their ever-flying momentum;
the blue seas surely know the height from which they come.
Again, he cited the case of Baoshou opening the hall. Sansheng pushed forward a monk, and Baoshou struck him immediately.
Sansheng said, "To act as a teacher in this manner is to blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhinzhou. The Master said: "Baoshou held the Mohe sword in his hand;
when the correct command was being executed, that monk saw the righteousness and acted with courage, returning home with the reward. Do you all wish to see Sansheng? From...
The sweating horses that came have no one to recognize them; we simply wish to re-examine their epoch-making merit.
That evening, he gave a small discourse: "An eighty-year-old grandfather rolls a brocade ball; who would have known that rolling it brings such joyful ease?
Now, having reached the summit of Lingxiao Peak, the clouds fly high and the waters flow on their own. At the places where he traveled in years past, there were stones, both large and small."
It remains as it was. Returning today once more, where are the high and low towers and pavilions?

Deshan’s staff fell like a rain of points; Linji’s shout surged like rolling thunder. Under the gate of Mount Jing, neither is of any use. Why? Because even with strong arms, one still finds the bow’s draw too weak;
even with clear eyes, one still recognizes the towering clouds of battle.
Again, he raised the topic: "The Way of the Three Sages is: 'When I meet people, I come forth; when I come forth, I do not act for the sake of others.
The Way of Xinghua is: 'When I meet people, I do not come forth; when I come forth, I immediately act for the sake of others. The Master offered this verse:
Hand in hand, they ascend the high tower, Singing and clapping, each responding to the other. When the song and drums end, all are drunk; There is neither joy nor sorrow.

Ascending the hall upon the conclusion of the retreat: This morning is the fifteenth day of the seventh month. The staff of the patch-robed monk dances, its head reaching toward the Western Heaven while its feet tread upon the Eastern Land.
It travels through a hundred cities without moving a single inch. A-he-he! Where the white clouds part, the green mountains are revealed.
Cai was lecturing on the scriptures when the news of Xi’s passing arrived. He ascended the hall and cited Dao Wu’s instruction to the assembly, saying: "Exaltedness does not lie in the highest peak;
wealth does not lie in Fuyan; joy does not lie in heaven; suffering does not lie in hell. Acquaintances fill the world."
"How many people can truly know the mind? Later, Dahui said: "Jingshan was not like this: 'Elevation is at the mountain peak;
wealth is at Fuyan; joy is in heaven; suffering is in hell. Who knows that beneath the scholar's hat is none other than the person from of old?
The Master said: "Of these two great elders, one traveled by boat and the other arrived on foot. Meeting on a narrow path, they raised their brows."
A laugh. Why? "When wine meets a kindred spirit, it is drunk; when a poem meets one who understands, it is chanted.
Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall: Heaven has no four walls, and the great earth serves as the furnace. At the edge of the hedge, the *bīlùsì* flute blows; a lone cry from a cold wild goose.
Had the Old Barbarian not crossed the river, there would be not a single spark of the fire's seed to this day.

On the anniversary of Master Wude’s death, he ascended the hall and, pointing with his whisk, said: Where the *uṇa* grass is lush and green, the mountain rises high and clouds hang halfway down its slopes.
Thorny brambles grow on every side; few are the travelers who venture there. Fifty years have passed in silence; what was right yesterday is not wrong today.
